marks.gloss_en: ולוקמה כולה כרבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון! -- why need Beit Shammai for the firstborn clause?
דילמא עד כאן לא קאמר רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון התם אלא פסולי המוקדשין דאלימי למיתפס פדיונו, אבל בכור דלא אלים למיתפס פדיונו -- לא
ורבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון לית ליה כל פסולי המוקדשין נמכרין באיטליז ונשקלין בליטרא? אלמא דכיון דאיכא רווחא להקדש שרי לה! (with p_revach_lehekdesh_shari)
the mishna: all disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the market and weighed by the litra
מה שמשביח בעור -- פוגם בבשר (= p_rav_mari_pogem_babasar): there is no net gain
במערבא משמיה דרבינא אמרי: מפני שנראה כעובד עבודה בקדשים (= p_ravina_oved_avoda)
Rav Mari son of Rav Kahana: what [skinning from the feet] improves in the hide, it damages in the meat
גזירה שמא יגדל מהן עדרים עדרים (= p_ryba_gezera_adarim)
R' Yosei bar Avin: a decree, lest he raise flocks upon flocks from them
R' Yehuda: a firstborn seized by [excess] blood -- even if it will die, one does not let its blood
if one is liable for cutting, for detaching is he not all the more so? -- so the verse's 'detached' is free to include detaching after cutting
[all agree] that one who castrates after another has castrated is liable
דתניא: מנין שלא יביא דבילה ובצק ויניחנה על האוזן... תלמוד לומר כל מום (kind tanya_kevatei for דתניא, under protest)
and the Rabbanan too -- is it not written 'no blemish at all shall be in it'? (a bare verse; kind svara for want of a verse-objection kind)
לגרמא הוא דאתי -- it comes to forbid causing a blemish indirectly (= p_kol_mum_lgrama)
for Rabbanan, 'any blemish' comes to forbid causing a blemish indirectly

ממאי? perhaps R' Meir forbids only where one blemishes by direct action, but in the barrel case, where impurity comes by grama, holds like R' Yehoshua; and R' Eliezer guards the barrel only because perhaps Elijah will purify it, but where the firstborn would certainly die if left he holds like the Rabbanan (33b.11-12)
perhaps the Rabbanan permit only here, where if left it dies; but there, perhaps Elijah will purify it -- they hold like R' Eliezer

perhaps R' Yehuda forbids only here, where one acts directly; there, by grama, he holds like R' Yehoshua; and Rabban Gamliel says do nothing only because perhaps Elijah will purify it, but here, where if left it dies, he holds like the Rabbanan (33b.13-14)
ועוד, הכא בקראי פליגי והכא בקראי פליגי -- the bloodletting tannaim dispute over Lev 22:21 (R' Yochanan, 33b.15-17) and the teruma tannaim over Num 18:8 (34a.2-6); the two disputes are not one
all agree that one who leavens [a meal-offering] after another has leavened it is liable
and R' Meir -- what does he do with 'perfect shall it be to be accepted'?
(first answer, abandoned) for R' Meir, 'perfect shall it be' excludes an animal blemished from the outset
it excludes disqualified consecrated animals after redemption (= p_tamim_psulei_hamukdashin); the first answer, a born-blemished animal (33b.18), fell to פשיטא, דיקלא בעלמא הוא (33b.19)

rather, for R' Meir it excludes disqualified consecrated animals after their redemption -- one would think that since they remain forbidden for shearing and labour they are forbidden to blemish too; it teaches otherwise
R' Meir: one may let a congested firstborn's blood in a place where the cut makes no blemish
Chachamim: one may let its blood even in a place where the cut makes a blemish
as the dispute here [over bloodletting the firstborn], so the dispute over the barrel of teruma
R' Yehoshua: if in a concealed place he may move it to an exposed one, if covered he may uncover it
R' Meir [no bloodletting where it blemishes] holds like R' Eliezer [guard the barrel]
they [the bloodletting tannaim] disputed only one who inflicts a blemish on an already-blemished animal
